name: synthetic graph generator study
description: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved great success on a node classification task. Despite the broad interest in developing and evaluating GNNs, they have been assessed with limited benchmark datasets. As a result, the existing evaluation of GNNs lacks fine-grained analysis from various characteristics of graphs. Motivated by this, we conduct extensive experiments with a synthetic graph generator that can generate graphs having controlled characteristics for fine-grained analysis. Our empirical studies clarify the strengths and weaknesses of GNNs from four major characteristics of real-world graphs with class labels of nodes, i.e., 1) class size distributions (balanced vs. imbalanced), 2) edge connection proportions between classes (homophilic vs. heterophilic), 3) attribute values (biased vs. random), and 4) graph sizes (small vs. large). In addition, to foster future research on GNNs, we publicly release our codebase that allows users to evaluate various GNNs with various graphs
typical_sota_score: varies widely: typically high (≈85–95%) on balanced, homophilic synthetic graphs and substantially lower (≈50–75%) on heterophilic, imbalanced, or biased-attribute settings
reputation: A research benchmark used in the GNN literature for controlled synthetic analysis, but not a widely standardized community leaderboard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; primarily used for fine-grained analysis of GNN behavior under controlled graph properties rather than a single canonical leaderboard score.
